system_overview: This specification models a generic ring buffer (circular buffer) data structure used as the foundation for the Disruptor inter-thread communication pattern. The ring buffer has a fixed number of slots, each of which can hold a value. It provides read and write operations with tracking of which threads are currently accessing each slot, enabling detection of data races between producer and consumer threads.
actors_and_components: The ring buffer is parameterized by a set of reader threads, a set of writer threads, a fixed size, a set of permissible values, and a null sentinel value. Readers perform multi-step read operations (begin read, read value, end read) and writers perform multi-step write operations (write value, end write). The ring buffer itself does not define a complete system specification; it is a reusable component intended to be instantiated by higher-level specifications.
state_variables: The ring buffer tracks three things for each slot (indexed from zero to one less than the buffer size): (1) the value currently stored in the slot (initially null), (2) the set of readers currently accessing the slot, and (3) the set of writers currently accessing the slot.
initial_state: All slots contain the null value. No readers are accessing any slot. No writers are accessing any slot.
actions: The ring buffer provides the following operations: (1) Write: a writer writes a value to a slot at a given index, simultaneously adding itself to that slot's writer set and updating the slot's stored value. (2) End write: a writer removes itself from a slot's writer set, indicating it has finished writing. (3) Begin read: a reader adds itself to a slot's reader set, indicating it is beginning to read. (4) Read: returns the value currently stored at a given index (a pure query with no state change). (5) End read: a reader removes itself from a slot's reader set, indicating it has finished reading. An index-of operator maps a sequence number to a slot index using modular arithmetic (sequence number modulo buffer size).
safety_properties: The no-data-races invariant requires that for every slot: (a) the set of active readers and the set of active writers are never both non-empty at the same time (no simultaneous read and write to the same slot), and (b) at most one writer is accessing any given slot at a time. A type invariant ensures that slot values are either null or a member of the value set, reader sets are subsets of the reader set parameter, and writer sets are subsets of the writer set parameter.
liveness_properties: NOT_SPECIFIED. The ring buffer module defines no temporal properties; liveness requirements are specified by the higher-level modules that instantiate it.
model_bounds: The buffer size, reader set, writer set, value set, and null value are all declared as constants to be supplied by the instantiating module. The buffer size must be a positive natural number. The writer and reader sets must be non-empty. The null value must not be a member of the value set.
additional_assumptions: This module is designed as a reusable library component, not a standalone specification. It uses local imports (not exported to instantiating modules). The data race invariant is expected to be asserted by any specification that uses this ring buffer. The module does not define an initial state, next-state relation, or specification formula on its own; those are provided by the higher-level Disruptor specifications that instantiate it.
